public_rationale: MIT Technology Review published a July 30 article about attacks that trick AI models into bypassing restrictions. This establishes the attributed reporting. Some techniques discussed were discovered earlier, so the evidence supports fresh reporting rather than a claim that every technique originated that day. Whether the examples are disturbing remains a judgment.
limitations: This assessment verifies the publication and its subject, not the article's broader scientific conclusions.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: MIT Technology Review reported new jailbreaking adventures, which Marcus calls disturbing.

statement.excerpt: MIT Technology Review reported new, disturbing adventures in jailbreaking
statement.document_title: The seven most shambolic things that happened in AI today.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that MIT Technology Review recently published reporting about AI jailbreak methods or incidents.
New refers to the reporting and developments it describes; it need not mean every technique was first discovered that day.
Disturbing is the author's evaluation, not a separately measurable claim.
The July 31 roundup and adjacent July 30 material identify July 30–31 as the publication window.
criteria.support_condition: A dated MIT Technology Review article in the identified window reports AI jailbreak methods or incidents.
criteria.contradiction_condition: The identified article or a reliable publisher correction establishes that the report was not about AI jailbreaking or was wrongly attributed.
